summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop after heavy decoder batch jobs introduced — suspected GPU thermal throttling and autoscaler mis-sizing
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sustained throughput degradation and increased p95 token latency on their Dedicated reservation in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC. Impact: Customer application experienced 5–10x increase in tail latency and intermittent 504s; user-facing features degraded. Environment: Dedicated pool id rp-dedicated-44 (us-west-2), running mixed workload: interactive chat (short tokens) plus new nightly batched decoder jobs submitted by customer as long-running, high-LM-step requests. Observed start: 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC. Expected: stable p95 < 300ms for interactive workloads. Observed: p95 spiking to 2.1s, token throughput down ~60%.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route interactive requests and heavy batched decoder requests to the dedicated pool (rp-dedicated-44) 2) Submit concurrent long-sequence batched requests (seq_len ~4096) at low qps but long-running decoder steps 3) Observe autoscaler behavior, node GPU utilization, and p95 latency on per-route dashboard
logs:
[2026-03-11T22:05:12Z] node-07 gpu0 util=92% temp=86C clock_throttle=1
[2026-03-11T22:07:01Z] scheduler queue_length=38 head_of_line=interactive_route
[2026-03-11T22:09:33Z] autoscaler decision: no_scale (thresholds: instance_cpu=40%, gpu_util_avg=48%)
[2026-03-11T22:10:00Z] api 504 route=interactive_route token_latency_p95=2100ms
investigation_notes: SRE pulled node telemetry for rp-dedicated-44 between 2026-03-11 21:50 and 2026-03-12 00:00 UTC — observed repeated episodes of GPU clocks dropping and sustained temps in mid-80sC on node-07 and node-08.
Serving runtime traces show long-running decoder slots held on GPUs for >30s per request for batched jobs; KV cache had few hits for these requests causing more compute per token.

Autoscaler configured to scale on instance count / CPU rather than GPU utilization; when batch jobs are low qps but long-running, CPU remained moderate while GPU saturated — autoscaler did not add capacity.
Scheduler logs show head-of-line queueing: interactive short requests queued behind large decoder batches because routing policy uses single shared queue per GPU when job_mix=heterogeneous.
No evictions or OOMs observed; this looks like contention and thermal/clock throttling under sustained heavy workloads rather than memory pressure.
Customer confirmed they deployed a nightly batch that increased average sequence length from ~512 to ~4096 starting 2026-03-11 evening.
current_hypothesis: Throughput regression caused by combination of (1) heterogeneous job mix with long-lived decoder batches causing head-of-line queueing, (2) autoscaler not reacting because it uses CPU/instance metrics instead of GPU-utilization, and (3) sustained GPU temperatures triggering clock throttling on specific nodes, reducing overall token throughput.
mitigation_steps_taken: Temporarily added capacity: manual scale +2 nodes to rp-dedicated-44 at 2026-03-12T02:15Z to relieve queue pressure.
Applied emergency scheduler policy change: enable preferential scheduling for interactive_route to avoid head-of-line blocking (fair-slot preemption) at 2026-03-12T02:28Z.
Advised customer to pause the nightly heavy decoder job as a stop-gap while we analyze deeper (customer confirmed pause at 2026-03-12T03:05Z).
next_steps: Run controlled repro in staging using customer job mix to validate head-of-line queueing and GPU thermal behavior (assigned to Marco).
Implement autoscaler experiment to add GPU-utilization as a scaling signal for dedicated pools — PR proposal in review (see related_github_prs).
Replace two affected nodes (node-07, node-08) from prod rotation and run thermal/firmware checks; collect vendor telemetry.
Schedule follow-up with PromptlyAI engineering to discuss longer-term isolation options: dedicated burst pool or queue prioritization in their routing rules.
resolution_notes: Partial mitigations applied (manual scale and scheduler change) restored interactive p95 to ~320ms with lower throughput variance. Customer paused heavy batch jobs. Pending full fix: autoscaler tuning and node hardware check. Will update when autoscaler PR merges and nodes validated.
